clue.text: Coventry rider keen to get back after game

indicators.note: after puts the reversed word behind the game in the answer

parts.note: go is a game, the Japanese board game

indicators.note: to get back says the word for keen is read backwards

parts.note: keen means avid, eager

explanation.surface: A cyclist from Coventry, eager to return to the track after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rider' suggests a cyclist or jockey, but Lady Godiva is the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry, an English city; 'to get back' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Lady Godiva rode a horse through the streets of Coventry, so she is its famous rider.

clue.text: German river's pronounced smell

indicators.note: pronounced says the river's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: the Oder is a river forming part of the German-Polish border

explanation.surface: A river in Germany is notorious for its stink.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, the plain dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Tetchy Gershwin's upsetting the Spanish writer

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George; with the 's that gives IRAS

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue turns the Spanish article and the pen upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the
a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An irritable Gershwin is annoying a Spanish author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' reverses both the Spanish article and the pen, giving CIBLE; Bic is a brand of ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Irascible and tetchy are synonyms, both meaning quick to anger.

clue.text: Highland beer (about 426ml)

indicators.note: about means the beer goes around the measure, wrapping it

parts.note: ale is a beer
a pint is about 568ml, so 426ml is three quarters of one: three of its four letters, PIN

explanation.surface: A beer from the Highlands, served in a three-quarter-pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: The 426ml is the trick: a pint is about 568ml, so three quarters of the word pint is its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine as an adjective describes high mountain land, so it fits highland used adjectivally.

clue.text: Back in Llandudno, bag a vintage Rover

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Back in a Welsh seaside town, someone picks up an old Rover car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters hidden in 'Llandudno, bag a vintage'; 'Back' reads them in reverse. Llandudno is a Welsh seaside resort; Rover was a British car make.
explanation.definitionFit: A rover is a wanderer, and a vagabond is a homeless wanderer.

clue.text: Very fresh nice calamari, line caught, European imported, popular dish

indicators.note: fresh says the combined letters are made anew in a different order
caught says the letter for line is taken into the pool of seafood letters being mixed
imported says the European letter is also brought into the pool being mixed

explanation.surface: A seafood menu boasting fresh calamari, line-caught and imported from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' and 'imported' bring L and E into the pool with NICE CALAMARI, and 'fresh' rearranges all of it after V.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is the most widely eaten ice cream flavour, so this dessert is a popular dish.

clue.text: Swallow feathers seen after shoot heads north

indicators.note: seen after puts the feathers behind the first piece
heads north in a down clue sends the word upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to plug someone is slang for to shoot them
down is soft fine feathers

explanation.surface: A swallow's feathers spotted after a shooting party moves north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' and 'feathers' suggest a bird, but Swallow is the verb; 'heads north' reverses the slang for shoot in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp down food or drink is to swallow it quickly.

clue.text: Bread roll using the French gas up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the pieces read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: le is French for the
gas and gab both mean idle chatter

explanation.surface: A French baker filling bread rolls with gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LE + GAB to BAGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled before baking.

clue.text: Discomfort one gets before going completely potty?

definitions.text: Discomfort one gets before going completely potty?

parts.words: Discomfort one gets before going completely potty?
parts.note: one is a toddler; going potty means being potty-trained, not going mad, and the soreness comes while still in nappies

explanation.walkthrough: 'going completely potty' reads as losing one's mind; here it is a toddler being fully potty-trained. A nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin irritation from wet nappies troubles babies until they are toilet-trained and stop wearing them.

clue.text: New Orleans? Pal, it can get pretty hot!

indicators.note: New, read apart from the city name, says the letters are made new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells a friend that New Orleans can get very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks part of the city's name but is the anagram signal, rearranging ORLEANS PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar panel sits in direct sunshine and can heat up considerably, hence it gets pretty hot.

clue.text: French 4 town by opening to enormous chasm

indicators.note: by sets the letter beside the town

parts.note: 4 is ALPINE, and Gap is a town in the French Alps

indicators.note: opening to means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A French mountain town sits near the opening to an enormous chasm.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' points to the answer at 4-down, ALPINE, so GAP is the Alpine French town; E is the first letter of 'enormous'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, so it can stand for a yawning chasm.

clue.text: Biscuit 23 unveils every now and again

parts.note: 23 is CLEAVAGE, a split, which is a crack

indicators.note: every now and again picks letters at intervals, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A cleavage revealed now and then, alongside a biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' sends the solver to 23-across, CLEAVAGE, whose split sense supplies the first piece; 'every now and again' takes the even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cracknel is a light, crisp kind of biscuit.

clue.text: Daughter rejected Yale, beginning to stack shelves

indicators.note: rejected says the university's name is turned back on itself
beginning to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A daughter turns down Yale and starts work stacking shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses YALE to ELAY; 'Shelves' looks like a noun in the stacking picture, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve a plan is to put it off, so shelves means postpones.

clue.text: Cut willows back

indicators.note: back says the word is read backwards

parts.note: cricket bats are made of willow, so willows are bats

explanation.surface: Willow trees pruned back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses BATS. Cricket bats are traditionally made of willow wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A stab is a knife wound, a cut, and also to stab is to pierce with a blade.

clue.text: Prime minister getting Speaker's cuppa (and what it soothes)

indicators.note: Speaker's says the words are as spoken aloud, giving the sound of the title

parts.note: a cuppa is a cup of tea, and hot sweet tea is the traditional remedy for shock, together TEA SHOCK

explanation.surface: A prime minister gets a cup of tea, plus the ailment it relieves.
explanation.walkthrough: TAOISEACH is said roughly 'tee-shock'. Cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the title of the head of government of Ireland, its prime minister.

clue.text: A large bird — cuckoo — reflected in Nile landmark

parts.note: a swan is a large bird

indicators.note: reflected says the word appears as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A big bird and a cuckoo seen reflected in the Nile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' reverses MAD to DAM. 'cuckoo' looks like a second bird but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan Dam spans the Nile in southern Egypt, one of the river's best-known structures.

clue.text: Buffet and tea OK, about five. Something stronger?

indicators.note: about says the shuffled tea letters go around the numeral
to buffet is to batter, so the letters are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: At a buffet tea is fine around five, but you might want something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a meal but is the anagram signal, shuffling AND TEA OK around V.
explanation.definitionFit: Undiluted vodka is a much stronger drink than tea, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Leads in English Sunday papers: Old Italian Shot

indicators.note: leads in means the leading letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the press means the newspapers

explanation.surface: Headlines in the English Sunday papers: an old Italian was shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a shooting in the headline, but it is a small measure of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is a short, strong Italian coffee, served as a single or double shot.

clue.text: Retiring QC: 'Is Nero finally admitting this evidence in court?'

indicators.note: Retiring says the hidden letters are read backwards
admitting says the quoted words take the answer in, holding it among their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A retiring barrister asks whether Nero is finally admitting this evidence in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'admitting' in the definition; it is the hiding signal, and 'Retiring' reverses CISNEROF. A QC is a senior British barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic evidence is scientific proof prepared for use in a court of law.

clue.text: Unwrapping small pouch is a pain

indicators.note: unwrapping strips away the outside, so the outer letters are removed

parts.note: a sachet is a small sealed pouch

explanation.surface: Opening a tiny packet turns out to be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapping' removes S and T, the outer letters of SACHET.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Mate got married, keeled over creating a bit of a flap

indicators.note: keeled over in a down clue says the pieces are turned upside down, so they read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
to wed is to get married, wed being the past tense too

explanation.surface: A friend got married and then fainted, causing a bit of a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeled over' reverses PAL + WED. 'flap' reads as a panic, but it is a fold of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewlap is the loose fold of skin hanging from the throat of cattle, a flap of skin.

clue.text: Loan shark more confident United will come first

indicators.note: will come first puts United at the front

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
surer means more confident

explanation.surface: A loan shark is sure United will finish top.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, just as a loan shark does.

clue.text: Mount ski lift touring American city

indicators.note: Mount in a down clue means climb, so the pieces read upwards, backwards
touring says the lift goes round the American letter

parts.note: a T-bar is a kind of ski lift

explanation.surface: Riding a ski lift on tour around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts A inside T-BAR, giving TABAR; 'Mount' reverses that. 'Mount' looks like a mountain but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Conservative majority vote in 2016 involving a grand split

indicators.note: involving says the vote surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Leave won the majority in the UK's 2016 Brexit referendum
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A Tory reflects on the Brexit result and a huge national split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts A + G inside LEAVE. The 2016 vote was the UK referendum on leaving the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleavage is a division or sharp split, especially between groups.

clue.text: Being of one mind to ignore adult vice

indicators.note: to ignore says the adult letter is left out

parts.note: being of one mind is being agreed
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: Being single-minded means overlooking an adult's vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ignore' removes A from AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is one of the seven deadly sins, a classic vice.

clue.text: Swedish actress slipping off Oscar outfit

indicators.note: slipping off says the letter is shed from the end

parts.note: Greta Garbo was a Swedish film actress
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Swedish actress drops her Oscar and slips out of her costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipping off' removes O from GARBO. 'Oscar' looks like the award but is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing, a person's outfit.

clue.text: Son left holding revolting pet snake … it could get mum going up the wall!

definitions.text: it could get mum going up the wall!

indicators.note: holding says the son and left letters wrap the reversed pet
revolting means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an adder is a snake

explanation.surface: A boy's disgusting pet snake drives his mother up the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' turns pet backwards and 'holding' sets it between the son and left letters. 'going up the wall' looks like losing her temper; here mum literally climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone climbs a stepladder to reach high on a wall, say when decorating.

clue.text: Online forum charm 'too manufactured'

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An internet forum where charm is dismissed as too contrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat room is a website area where users exchange messages, a kind of online forum.

clue.text: In which it is reported Nureyev finally appears in designer label?

indicators.note: appears in says that letter is set inside the label

parts.note: Prada is an Italian fashion house

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the dancer's name

explanation.surface: Is it reported that Nureyev finally turns up wearing designer clothes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' puts V, the last letter of Nureyev, inside PRADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Pravda was the Soviet Communist Party's newspaper, and news is reported in a paper.
